title: TIN MAN
think3:
something fell. I felt it fall.
...was it me?
law: 1st LAW — A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm.
photo: a dusty photo: a man and a boy.
doorEar: the door will not open. something ticks nearby...
endB: brain, eye, ear — and whatever you chose to take. down there the city has no law and no sun.
cityThought:
there is no ceiling.
and still, something out here weighs more than the lab did.
womanMonster: MONSTER! IT'S THE MONSTER FROM THE LAB!

I did nothing.
I only walked out.

she knows what I am.
I don't.

two ways.
one climbs the side of the building.
the other goes down, and the bottom isn't visible.
mouthDesc: a horn in the trash. it will do.
thinkMouth1: there is air moving through me now.
thinkMouth2:
I did not decide to say that.
where did that sentence come from?
legsDesc: springs. the ground is further away.
thinkLegs1:
the joints gave.
not broke — gave.
thinkLegs2:
I can reach higher.
and fall from higher.
thinkBoth:
springs and a horn.
I am assembling a body out of what the city threw away.
detSee: so it was true. the old man really built one of these.

he doesn't run.
he's the first one who doesn't run from me.

sheAnswer: YET. get that thing off my street.
thinkFlee:
I can't get past him.
and behind me is only the street that threw me out.
there's the hole.
act2Sub: where the city keeps what it won't look at
thinkUnder1:
there are stone columns down here.
this is older than the city.

nobody screams.
nobody runs.

thief1: easy. I've seen worse come down that hole.
thief2: you've been running since you left, haven't you. it's in the way you walk.
thief3: down here running gets you nowhere. there's nowhere to go.

he speaks to me.
not about me. to me.

whoever holds can be pulled along.
